big_idea: Canadian coins up to 50¢: nickel, dime, quarter, 50¢. They have DIFFERENT VALUES.
learning_intention: We are learning to name coins up to 50¢ and their values.
student_learning_goal: I can name coins up to 50¢ and their values.
success_criteria: I can SAY each coin's VALUE.
I can SORT coins by value.
I can FIND a coin by value.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Penny the Penguin — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.hook: Penny the Penguin: Friends, welcome to my market! Today I'll show you 4 Canadian COINS — nickel, dime, quarter, 50¢.
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Penny the Penguin Shopkeeper puppet (felt penguin in apron). 'Shoppers — I'm Penny! In my market we use COINS. Today we meet 4 coins!'

Define VALUE first. 'VALUE = how much money is worth.'

Reveal each coin one by one with the chart:

NICKEL: 5¢. Silver. BEAVER on the back. 'Nickel = 5 cents!'
DIME: 10¢. Silver but SMALLER. BOAT on the back. 'Dime = 10 cents! It's the SMALLEST coin even though it's worth MORE than nickel!'
QUARTER: 25¢. Silver. CARIBOU on the back. 'Quarter = 25 cents!'
50¢: 50¢. Silver. Coat of arms on the back. 'Half-dollar = 50 cents!'

'Penny says — every coin has its own VALUE. The PICTURE on the back tells you which coin!'

Demo. 'I'll hold up a coin. You name it!' Hold up nickel. Class: 'NICKEL!' Hold up dime. Class: 'DIME!'

Now show the trick. 'The DIME is SMALLER than the nickel but worth MORE. Be careful — size doesn't tell value!'

Show sorting. 'Sort coins by VALUE: nickel (5¢) → dime (10¢) → quarter (25¢) → 50¢.'

Now each pair gets the Coin Cards. They sort all 20 coin cards into 4 piles by name.

'Penny says — coin name = coin VALUE!'

steps.instruction: Hand out Coin Cards. Pairs sort by NAME (4 piles).
Resort by VALUE — smallest to largest.
Help by pointing to chart for size vs value.

differentiation.for_movement_learners: Walk to 4 stations, one per coin.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Five signals: names; values; sorts; size-vs-value; consistency.

discussion_prompts: Which is BIGGEST: nickel or dime?
Which is WORTH MORE: nickel or dime?
What's the value of a quarter?
consolidation.exit_routine: Each child shares ONE: 'A ___ is worth ___ cents.'

assessment_in_this_lesson.evidence_collected: Tracker of coin naming and values.
assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 1 sets the baseline for coin identification.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child says NICKEL is worth more than DIME because it's bigger — repairing the size-vs-value trap at Grade 1
expanded_walkthrough.rationale: Most common Grade-1 trap on F1.1: child uses physical size to judge value. Nickel is BIGGER than dime but worth LESS.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Coin sort. Child says nickel is worth more because it's bigger.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Penny asks — let's check the chart. Nickel = ___. Dime = ___.'

Probe. 'Nickel = 5¢. Dime = 10¢. So dime is WORTH MORE even though it's SMALLER.'

Generalise. 'Penny says — SIZE doesn't tell VALUE. The number tells value!'

If still confused: stack 2 nickels = 10¢. 'Dime by itself = 10¢. So 1 dime = 2 nickels.'
common_misconceptions: Bigger coin = more value. (Repair: check chart.)
Smallest coin = least value. (Repair: dime is exception.)
recovery_moves: Drill 'check the value, not the size'.

parts_outline.task: Match each coin to its value.
Circle the coin worth MORE in 3 pairs.
